 Appearance :
 For the Appellant/s : Mr.Rajiv Kumar, Adv.
 For the State : Mr.Zeyaul Hoda, App
 For the Vigilance Dept. : Mr.Arvind Kumar, Adv.

======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Singh
Oral Order
2 03-02-2026 1-Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned APP representing the State and learned counsel for the Vigilance Department.

2-Admit.
3-Summon the lower Court record in connection with Special Case No.94 of 2002, arising out of Vigilance Police Station Case No.007 of 2000 from the concerned trial Court.
4-This appeal under Sections 415 (2) and 430 (1) of B.N.S.S. has been preferred by the appellant namely Ajay Kumar Srivastava against the judgment of conviction dated 10.12.2025 and order of sentence dated 18.12.2025 passed by learned Special Judge, Vigilance, North Bihar, Muzaffarpur, in Special Case No.94 of 2002, arising out of Vigilance Police Patna High Court CR.

477(A), 120(B), 109, 201 of the IPC and section 13(2) read with section 13(1) (d) of Prevention of Corruption Act, District Muzaffarpur, convicting the appellant u/s 13(2) read with section 13(1)(d) of Prevention of Corruption Act and sentencing him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs.25,000/- and in default of payment of fine, additional simple imprisonment for three months.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the appellant is not sustainable in the eyes of the law.

It is further submitted that the trial Court in exercise of powers under Section 389 (3) of Cr.P.C. has granted provisional bail to the appellant vide order dated 18.12.2025, which has not been misused by him and instant Criminal Appeal has been preferred within limitation period.
The appellant does not have any criminal history to his credit.
Lastly, it is submitted that in case provisional bail of appellant is confirmed, he will not misuse the Patna High Court CR.
APP ( SJ) No.117 of 2026(2) dt.03-02-2026 liberty of bail
and will co-operate in early hearing of this appeal

. 
7-Per contra, learned A.P.P. for the State and learned counsel for the Vigilance Department opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant by contending that prosecution has proved it's case beyond reasonable doubt.

8-Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that appellant has been convicted for a maximum period of three years, and against which he has served 17 days in jail.
Due to heavy docket, this criminal appeal is not likely to be heard in near future.
There is no material on record to presume that there is danger, of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail to the appellant.

9-Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and the reasons as mentioned above, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant is liable to be released on bail during pendency of this Criminal Appeal.
Hence provisional bail granted to the appellant as noted above is made confirmed and he shall be treated on bail during pendency of this case.
10-The sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.117 of 2026(2) dt.03-02-2026 during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal.

11-The appellant shall furnish fresh personal bond and bail bond of two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned within two weeks from today, failing which the liberty of bail shall automatically stands revoked and he shall be taken into custody.
12-On acceptance of the personal bond and bail bonds, the concerned court below shall furnish the photocopy thereof to this Court for being kept on record of this Criminal Appeal.
13-Let this Criminal Appeal be listed in due course for hearing.

(Sanjay Kumar Singh , J) pallavi/-
